Employee HR Policy

General Workplace, Attendance & Leave Policy

Purpose

This fictional policy provides general guidelines for employee attendance, working hours, leave, and workplace
responsibilities. It is intended as a sample document for OCR, chunking, embedding, ChromaDB, and retrieval testing.

1. Working Hours

The standard working schedule is Monday through Friday. Employees are expected to work eight hours per day,
excluding approved meal breaks. Employees should report to work on time and remain available during scheduled
working hours.

2. Attendance

Employees are responsible for recording attendance through the approved attendance system. Repeated late arrival,
early departure, or unexplained absence may result in attendance follow-up. Employees unable to attend work should
inform their manager as early as possible.

3. Leave Policy

1002.text:
3. Leave Policy

Employees may request casual leave, sick leave, or annual leave according to company rules. Leave requests should
normally be submitted before the requested absence. Managers may consider staffing requirements and business
priorities when reviewing requests.

4. Sick Leave

Employees who cannot work because of illness should notify their manager promptly. Where company rules require
supporting documentation for extended absence, the employee must provide it through the appropriate HR process.

5. Unplanned Absence

If an unexpected situation prevents an employee from reporting to work, the employee should contact the manager or
designated attendance contact as soon as possible. Failure to communicate an absence may result in attendance
review.

6. Leave Approval

Submitting a leave request does not automatically mean the leave is approved. Employees should confirm approval
before making commitments that depend on the leave being granted.

1003.text:
Employee HR Policy — Page 2

Work From Home, Conduct & Information Security

7. Work From Home

Work-from-home arrangements may be permitted when the employee's role, business needs, and team requirements
allow it. Remote employees must remain available during agreed working hours, attend scheduled meetings, and
complete assigned work on time.

8. Remote Work Responsibilities

Employees working remotely are responsible for maintaining a suitable work environment, protecting company
information, and using approved communication and collaboration tools.

9. Workplace Conduct

Employees are expected to behave professionally and respectfully toward colleagues, customers, contractors, and
business partners. Harassment, intimidation, threats, discrimination, abusive communication, and deliberate disruption
are not acceptable.

10. Confidentiality

1004.text:
10. Confidentiality

Employees may access confidential business, employee, customer, financial, or technical information. Such
information must only be accessed and shared for legitimate business purposes and according to company
procedures.

11. Information Security

Company devices, accounts, passwords, documents, and systems must be protected from unauthorized access.
Employees should not share passwords. Suspicious emails, unauthorized access, lost devices, or possible data
exposure should be reported to IT or the security contact.

12. Company Resources

Company equipment, software, internet access, and communication systems are provided primarily for business
activities. Employees must not intentionally introduce malicious software, bypass security controls, or use systems for
unauthorized activities.

13. Employee Records

1005.text:
13. Employee Records

Employees should keep personal and employment information submitted to HR accurate and current. Changes to
contact information, emergency contacts, banking information, or required records should be reported through the
approved HR process.

1006.text:
Employee HR Policy — Page 3

Performance, Grievance, Discipline & Separation

14. Performance Reviews

Employee performance may be reviewed periodically against role responsibilities, objectives, quality expectations,
teamwork, and business outcomes. Managers should provide feedback and discuss areas requiring support or
improvement.

15. Performance Improvement Plan

When performance does not meet expected standards, the company may establish a performance improvement plan.
The plan may identify performance gaps, expected outcomes, support or training, review dates, and the period
available for improvement.

16. Employee Grievance

Employees with a workplace concern should use the appropriate reporting channel where practical. A grievance may
relate to workplace conduct, management practices, working conditions, policy concerns, or other employment
matters. HR may review the concern and request information.

17. Disciplinary Action

1007.text:
17. Disciplinary Action

Failure to follow company policies or workplace requirements may result in corrective or disciplinary action depending
on the seriousness of the matter. Actions may include counseling, written warning, suspension where permitted, or
termination, subject to company procedures and applicable law.

18. Resignation

An employee who chooses to resign should submit a formal resignation through the approved process. The applicable
notice period is determined by the employment agreement and company rules. Employees should support an orderly
transition during the notice period.

19. Exit Process

Before leaving the organization, employees may be required to return company property, complete an exit interview,
transfer documents and responsibilities, and complete clearance activities. Final settlement will follow applicable
company procedures and legal requirements.

20. Policy Administration

1008.text:
20. Policy Administration

HR may update, clarify, or replace policy provisions when business requirements, company procedures, or applicable
laws change. Employees should refer to the latest approved version and contact HR when clarification is required.
